title: Traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation: a case study of nonoperative management in a mixed martial arts athlete.
journal: The Journal of the Canadian Chiropractic Association

sections.label: OBJECTIVE
sections.text: To present an evidence-informed approach to the nonoperative management of a first-time, traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation.

sections.label: CLINICAL FEATURES
sections.text: A 30-year-old mixed martial arts athlete, with no prior shoulder injuries, presented one day following a first-time, traumatic anterior shoulder dislocation. An eight-week, individualized, intensive, nonoperative rehabilitation program was immediately begun upon presentation.

sections.label: INTERVENTION AND OUTCOME
sections.text: Management consisted of immobilization of the shoulder in external rotation and a progressive rehabilitation program aimed at restoring range of motion, strength of the dynamic stabilizers, and proprioception of the shoulder. Eight weeks post-dislocation the patient had regained full range of motion and strength compared to the unaffected limb and apprehension and relocation tests for instability were negative.

sections.label: CONCLUSION
sections.text: This case illustrates successful management of a first-time, traumatic, anterior shoulder dislocation using immobilization in external rotation combined with an intensive rehabilitation program.
